title: Competency Mapping with Bloom’s Taxonomy: A Solution for Quantifying Cognitive Depth
content: Contribution: This article presents a method that combines academic performance, Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy, and the curriculum structure to map competency profiles developed by students within an engineering curriculum. Background: In Brazil, engineering education is undergoing a major shift from content-based to competency-based curricula. This transformation brings significant challenges, especially regarding pedagogical redesign and the quantitative assessment of skills and capabilities aligned with market expectations. Intended Outcomes: To present the construction of competency profiles from the collected data and examine the comparison indicators obtained in the application to the program under study. Application Design: The framework integrates graph theory, data preprocessing techniques, and software engineering to process academic performance data. It was implemented in a Computer Engineering program, using academic records of students who had completed at least 90% of the program’s coursework. Findings: In the application presented, academic grades and Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy levels selected by instructors were processed to generate indicators for comparing competency profiles. These results illustrate how the method operates on the dataset analyzed.
